en: Using a ramp reduces the force needed to push a heavy wheelchair, preventing caregiver back injuries.
Wearing rubber-soled shoes increases friction with wet floors, preventing dangerous slips and falls.
Storing heavy boxes on lower shelves prevents gravitational potential energy from turning into dangerous kinetic energy if they fall.
Keeping strong magnets away from medical pacemakers prevents magnetic interference with the device's life-saving electrical signals.
Never touch electrical switches with wet hands because water conducts electricity and can cause severe bodily shocks.
Wearing sunglasses with UV protection blocks harmful ultraviolet light from damaging the delicate tissues of your eyes.
Wearing earplugs near loud construction equipment reduces sound energy entering your ears, preventing permanent hearing damage.
Using cloth oven mitts provides thermal insulation that prevents heat from burning your hands when holding hot pots.
Plugging too many appliances into one extension cord creates excess heat energy, which can start an electrical fire.
Applying oil to a rusty bicycle chain reduces harmful friction, making pedaling easier and preventing sudden chain breaks.
Using a wheelbarrow as a second-class lever multiplies your lifting force, preventing muscle strain when moving heavy rocks.
Never leave a burning candle unattended because the chemical energy in the wax continuously converts to dangerous heat energy.
